stableMappingPatterns.name: Notional -> tradeLot.quantity
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Notional amounts (value + currency) in FpML are repeatedly represented as a tradeLot quantity in the CDM with numeric value and currency unit.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: Trade-level economic size is preserved by mapping FpML notional constructs to CDM tradeLot.quantity which captures amount+currency.
caveats: Requires both numeric initialValue and an associated currency to form a CDM quantity.
FpML notional schedule variants (steps, long-stub) may require aggregation or selection logic not captured by a single rule.

stableMappingPatterns.name: Swap stream payer/receiver -> interestratepayout.payerReceiver
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Party references used on swapStream elements are resolved into CDM payer/receiver roles on interest rate payouts.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: Each swapStream represents a side of the swap; mapping its party hrefs to payer/receiver yields the CDM representation of counterparty cashflow direction.
caveats: Representative examples show consistent href use, but derived CDM role labels (e.g., 'Party1') differ from FpML partyId values - mapping of identifiers is inconsistent across examples.

stableMappingPatterns.name: Strip timezone from effectivedate values
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Date/time strings in FpML that include timezone suffixes (e.g., trailing 'Z') are normalized by removing the timezone before populating CDM date fields.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: CDM date fields in examples use date-only or normalized datetime formats; removing trailing timezone characters produces the expected CDM format.
caveats: Normalization assumes UTC 'Z' suffix or similar trailing timezone tokens; other timezone encodings are not evidenced.
Time-of-day information is effectively lost when trimming to date-only representations.

stableMappingPatterns.name: Strip timezone from expirationdate values
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Expiration dates for options in FpML are normalized by removing timezone suffixes before mapping into CDM expiration date fields.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: CDM examples show expiration dates without the trailing timezone; the strip-normalize step produces consistent formatting expected by CDM.
caveats: Normalization is demonstrated on examples with trailing 'Z'; other timezone formats are not evidenced.
Ensure that business rules about timezone interpretation are satisfied before removing timezone info.

variantsAndExceptions.name: Party identifier label variance
variantsAndExceptions.description: CDM uses short role-like labels (e.g., 'Party1', 'Party2', 'PartyA') instead of FpML partyId values in examples.
variantsAndExceptions.impactOnGeneralization: Significant - mapping logic must allow for label generation or external enrichment; do not assume CDM.party.partyId equals FpML partyId.

variantsAndExceptions.name: Payer/receiver apparent inversion in option premium vs payout
variantsAndExceptions.description: Some swaption examples indicate that premium payer values in FpML do not always align with CDM optionPayout.payerReceiver mapping (possible inversion).
variantsAndExceptions.impactOnGeneralization: High - mapping of premium vs option payout roles must be validated case-by-case; do not apply an assumption of consistent direction without checks.

variantsAndExceptions.name: Trade identifier omission or substitution
variantsAndExceptions.description: FpML tradeId values (e.g., TW9235, TRN12000) are sometimes absent or replaced by different CDM tradeIdentifier values (e.g., SW2000).
variantsAndExceptions.impactOnGeneralization: Moderate - do not assume a 1:1 mapping for trade identifiers; mapping may require external provenance or enrichment.
